classification.difficultyReason: Read horizontal and vertical extents from supplied graphs, distinguish included extrema from excluded asymptotes, and express the disconnected domain in part (e) using 'or'.

content.prompt: State the domain and range of the following graphs.

spec.description: Vertical line at x=2 with both ends arrowed.

answer.worked: Every point has $x=2$. The line extends up and down indefinitely, so every real $y$ occurs. Therefore D: $x=2$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Horizontal line at y=−1 with both ends arrowed.

answer.worked: The line extends indefinitely left and right, and every point has $y=-1$. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $y=-1$.

spec.description: Reciprocal-shaped branches in quadrants I and III with four continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: Both coordinate axes are asymptotes; no numerical scale supplied.

answer.worked: The branches approach both coordinate axes without meeting them. Every nonzero horizontal and vertical value occurs. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$, $x\ne0$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$, $y\ne0$.

spec.description: Increasing S-shaped curve through the origin with dashed horizontal asymptotes ±π/2.
spec.mathematics: All real x; neither horizontal asymptote attained. Horizontal scale schematic.

answer.worked: The curve extends indefinitely left and right. It stays between $y=-\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $y=\frac{\pi}{2}$ without reaching either asymptote. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $-\frac{\pi}{2}<y<\frac{\pi}{2}$.

spec.description: Outward-opening branches symmetric about both axes, vertices at (−2,0) and (2,0).
spec.mathematics: Horizontal extents x≤−2 or x≥2; unrestricted vertical extent. Curvature schematic.

answer.worked: The left branch includes $x=-2$ and extends left; the right branch includes $x=2$ and extends right. Together the branches cover every real $y$-value. Therefore D: $x\le-2$ or $x\ge2$ and R: $y\in\mathbb R$.

spec.description: Symmetric bell-shaped curve with maximum at (0,1); tails approach dashed y=−1 from above.
spec.mathematics: Maximum 1 attained; lower limit −1 excluded; no horizontal scale supplied.

answer.worked: The curve extends indefinitely left and right. Its maximum $y=1$ is included, while the tails approach $y=-1$ without reaching it. Therefore D: $x\in\mathbb R$ and R: $-1<y\le1$.
